properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-11-04 to Xto Energy Inc in Chapman Twp, Clinton county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Xto Energy Inc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-11-04
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 867191
Permit API: 035-21316
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Chapman Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-11-04
Comments: I arrived on site and met Nate Veneziano, Clint Stoltzfus, and George Winebark of XTO. Zachary Lieb and Brynn Yochim of Moody & Associates were also present. Sitewide containment was being removed and the pad screened to identify areas in need of excavation due to the produced water release identified on 5/28/19 by Brad Kline, WQS for the Department. Containment removal began to the north of the wellheads, working clockwise around them. Zach and Brynn began their conductivity screening on the west edge of the pad where high conductance fluid was moving off the pad; distressed vegetation in this area appears to have recovered. Very little water was present on the north side of the wellheads, and soil and water conductance in this area was low (.2-.4 mS/cm) with the exception of an area bare of gravel approximately 10' east by northeast of the wells. This area showed soil conductance of 1.98 mS/cm. To the east of the wellheads, what appeared to be several petroleum stains were present, and one very small (less than 1 quart) puddle showed high conductance (16.50 mS/cm). Other puddles in close proximity showed low conductance (.65-1.2 mS/cm). To the south of the wells between the wells and the produced water Baker tank battery, water was puddled nearly everywhere; conductance reading were low (.185-.235 mS/cm). When I departed, containment had not yet been removed to the west of the wellheads; as this was the potential flow path of the release, this area should be screened thoroughly.

Comments: On 4/20/2026, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill at Minton William well pad in Independence Township, Beaver County. The spill reportedly occurred on 3/31/2026, at 4:15 PM. The spill was reportedly caused when a minor surge of gas caused produced water to release from the casing of well 11H to the graveled well pad, while the operator conducted work on well 11H. An estimated 10 gallons of produced water released and was contained to the graveled well pad. The operator reportedly remediated this release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1). The operator reported the spill to the Department on 3/31/2026, at 5:11 PM (IR 4172810). Accompanying the Department during this inspection is Range Resources representative Nate Smiell. Intermittently present was Range Resources representative Derek Zofchak. The Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) for this site was terminated on 10/13/2021.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, and new well permits are on site (photos 10-13). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Eight gas wells are onsite that appear to be equipped for production (photo 16). Well 11H is temporarily shut-in to accommodate the drill rig (photo 18). Smiell reported that well 13H is being drilled at the time of inspection (photo 8). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection (photo 4). The GPU/Vertical Separator Units are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photos 5 and 6). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022. All other storage containers and machinery on site that appear to contain regulated substances are placed within secondary containment (photos 9 and 14). The secondary containments on site appear to be in good condition at the time of inspection, with no observable holes or tears. No evidence of fluid releases, such as staining, was observed on the well pad surface during this inspection. The containment inspection log is available on site in the company trailer (photo 17). The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 2 and 3).Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be noted and immediately corrected against the 3/31/2026 spill.

I scraped a small area of gravel to assess the depth of staining and it appeared to be about two inches deep where I scraped. Operator, the Department requests that you inspect this area and contact the Department with your findings. Please ensure that your response is in accordance with 78a66. There were no erosional issues noted at the time of inspection. There are violations associated with this inspection.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr ¿Stepped¿ pressure build-up tests ¿SPBUT¿ being performed on all (6) wells on the CAPPUCCI pad. The CAPPUCCI 2H, N2H, 4H, N4H, 102H and HJMM WYO 1H wells. These tests are being performed in response to a new gas migration investigation in area underway by The Department. SPBUTs were initiated on 5/18/20 @ ~ 08:00 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - The CAPPUCCI 2H is a 2 string well, with (20¿x 9 5/8¿) and (9 5/8¿x 5 ½¿) annuli. - The HJMM WYO 1H and CAPPUCCI WYO N4H wells (20¿x 13 3/8¿) annulus has open casing top in cellar. Gas: 83 % (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened back to vent to production tanks @ 11:00. ** The presence of pressure and gas was detected in the (13x9) annuli of all the wells on the pad with the exception of the Cappucci Wyo 2H which is a (2) string well. This is indicative of defective cement which is a violation of Title 25-chapter 78a.86 - Defective casing or cementing. The Department requests, in writing by 7/01/20, how CALLC plans to comply with Ch. 78a.86.

Comments: On April 9, 2026, the Department conducted a Compliance Evaluation Inspection (CSE) at the Sproul well site in Stewart Township, Fayette County. This inspection also follows-up to the violation issued in IR 4140173 for failure to comply with the 5/01/2025 amendment of the 12/16/2021 CO and A. A Consent Order and Agreement (CO and A) was executed between the Department and the operator on 12/16/2021. The First Modification to the COA was entered on 5/01/2025. The 12/16/2021 CO and A states that the operator "shall restore the Sproul 7005 Site in accordance with the restoration plan in the expired Sproul ESCGP, including but not limited to the installation of all Post Construction Stormwater Management Best Management Practices ("PCSM BMPs"). Restoration of the Sproul 7005 Well Site shall be completed by 10/30/2025." The operator shall then "submit a Notice of Termination ("NOT") for the Sproul ESCGP once permanent vegetation has been established at the Well Site in accordance with 25 Pa. Code 102.7. The NOT shall be submitted to the Department no later than 12/31/2025.A Notice of Termination (NOT) request was submitted to the Department by the operator on December 31, 2025. A notarized Post-Drilling Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration and the updated map requested in IR 4085078 were submitted with the operator's NOT request on December 31, 2025.However, the Department observed possible soil cracking and developing soil displacement on the slope north of the well pad on January 5, 2026, at the time of IR 4119144. The operator reported on January 16, 2026, that they conducted repairs in this location and provided a photo of the repairs (IR 4128095). It appeared in the photo provided by the operator that the repair resulted in ground disturbances, as they applied temporary stabilization after completing their repairs. Therefore, the NOT request was denied on January 30, 2026 (IR 4133379). A violation was issued on February 10, 2026, for failure to comply with the 5/01/2025 amendment of the 12/16/2021 CO and A (IR 4140173). The following was observed during the inspection:Temporary stabilization is applied to the location where the potential soil cracking and developing soil displacement was observed, at the time of IR 4140173 (photos 11-19). Less than 70 % uniform and adequate vegetative growth is observable through the temporary stabilization. This location does not appear to threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth and/or well head integrity at the time of inspection. The potential soil cracking and developing soil displacement were not identifiable during this inspection. Therefore, this location may have re-stabilized since the time of IR 4140173. No evidence of further potential soil displacement was observable in this location. It appears that no restorative work has been conducted on site since the time of IR 4119144. The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 4 and 8). No evidence of loose sediment flows was observed at the locations of the Sediment Trap and access road stormwater culvert (photos 5-7 and 18-20). Some soil appears to have been removed from the soil stockpile, leaving an unvegetated area of disturbance (photo 11). The Department recommends that the operator mulch and seed this location. Violations may be forthcoming pending further review by the Department. If the disturbed topsoil pile was caused by a third-party, then the Department recommends that the operator document all third-party disturbances that occur on site, and take reasonable efforts to stop them and prevent accelerated erosion.The gas well is equipped with a well tag and the operator's information. No evidence of a fluid leak was observed to the ground around the gas well (photos 21 and 22).Based on observations from this inspection, the violation issued in IR 4140173 shall remain outstanding.

A notarized Post-Drilling Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration and the updated map requested in IR 4085078 were submitted with the operator's NOT request on December 31, 2025.However, the Department observed possible soil cracking and developing soil displacement on the slope north of the well pad on January 5, 2026, at the time of IR 4119144. The operator reported on January 16, 2026, that they conducted repairs in this location and provided a photo of the repairs (IR 4128095). It appeared in the photo provided by the operator that the repair resulted in ground disturbances, as they applied temporary stabilization after completing their repairs. Therefore, the NOT request was denied on January 30, 2026 (IR 4133379). A violation was issued on February 10, 2026, for failure to comply with the 5/01/2025 amendment of the 12/16/2021 CO and A (IR 4140173). The following was observed during the inspection:Temporary stabilization is applied to the location where the potential soil cracking and developing soil displacement was observed, at the time of IR 4140173 (photos 11-19). Less than 70 % uniform and adequate vegetative growth is observable through the temporary stabilization. This location does not appear to threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth and/or well head integrity at the time of inspection. The potential soil cracking and developing soil displacement were not identifiable during this inspection. Therefore, this location may have re-stabilized since the time of IR 4140173. No evidence of further potential soil displacement was observable in this location. It appears that no restorative work has been conducted on site since the time of IR 4119144. The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 4 and 8). No evidence of loose sediment flows was observed at the locations of the Sediment Trap and access road stormwater culvert (photos 5-7 and 18-20). Some soil appears to have been removed from the soil stockpile, leaving an unvegetated area of disturbance (photo 11). The Department recommends that the operator mulch and seed this location. Violations may be forthcoming pending further review by the Department. If the disturbed topsoil pile was caused by a third-party, then the Department recommends that the operator document all third-party disturbances that occur on site, and take reasonable efforts to stop them and prevent accelerated erosion.The gas well is equipped with a well tag and the operator's information. No evidence of a fluid leak was observed to the ground around the gas well (photos 21 and 22).Based on observations from this inspection, the violation issued in IR 4140173 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: Arrived onsite in response to reported release of diesel fuel. The release occurred on the eastern side of the pad near the pipeline that is run to the site. The release was reported as at least 5 gallons of fuel. The location of the release was not near containment used for the recent drilling onsite. The source and total volume of the release were unknown at the time of inspection.Mr. Dirt was onsite excavating the impacted soil. The initial area marked for excavation was approximately 8' by 10'. This increase in size was due in part to the stability of the excavated area causing the edges of the pit to break away. The impacted area was also excavated in a manner to ensure the complete removal of impacted soil.The removed material amounted to about 5 loads of soil that were 15 cubic yards per load. The soil was stored on secondary containment for the time being. Creston was also onsite collecting soil samples to verify that the remediation was sufficient.Based on the unknown volume of fuel released it is strongly recommended that Chesapeake remediate the location under Act 2 requirements. The result of this inspection Violations Noted for 78a56(a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b).

Unconventional: No
County: Elk

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-04-02
Comments: This inspection was performed following a report to the NWRO by Diversified Oil and Gas of a 25 gallon brine spill at their #38067 well. It appears as though a small leak formed in a 50 barrel poly tank over the winter, which allowed some production fluid to leach out slowly over time. Once the snow melted, the well tender noticed a small area (~10x10 ft) that had vegetation missing and deer prints. The diking was unlined, so it seems that production water had leached out, and high conductivity levels were noted in this area. All the brine stayed in a small area, and no waters are nearby to be a concern for migration. The operator has shut in this well for the time being, and excavation is scheduled for the week of 4/8. Continued inspection of this site will be performed at that time.

Inspection Date: 2019-09-03
Comments: Results from sample IDs 0718-101, 0718-102, and 0718-103, collected 8/19/2019 as documented in inspection report number 2922630, were received from the laboratory on 8/31/2019. At the time of inspection, a large volume of fluid was observed in the northeast corner of the pad surface and was discharging into the rock-lined stormwater channel, which begins at this corner of the pad, and flowing into the northeast infiltration basin. Conductivity of the fluid on the pad surface in the northeast corner of the pad had electrical conductivity (EC) readings between 4.61 mS/cm and 7.19 mS/cm. In the basin, the fluid entering from the channel had an EC of 5.85 mS/cm. Elevated levels of barium, strontium, and chlorides in samples 0718-101 and 0718-102, collected from the pad surface and the northeast infiltration basin, respectively, indicate that a discharge of a pollutional substance occurred. The discharge of a pollutional substance to the infiltration basin, considered Waters of the Commonwealth, is a violation of Section 401 of the Clean Streams Law. The volume of the release is underdetermined. The Department recommends following the process outlined in 78a66 in order to remediate the release. Violations noted. The violation cited on 8/26/2019 (IR #2925622) remains outstanding.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: MTN V OIL & GAS INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/30/2023
Violation Code: 102.22(a) - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to have site permanently stabilized and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation upon final completion of earth disturbance activity.
Violation ID: 8157507
Permit API: 005-27116
Unconventional: No
County: Armstrong
Municipality: Kittanning Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/05/2023
Comments: On Wednesday, 8/30/2023, I conducted a follow up inspection of the Mountain V Oil and Gas, Inc. P and N Coal, et al, 1 well, permit number 005-27116. The well is located in the woods off of Dam Road in Kittanning township, Armstrong county. Inspection #3580553, conducted on 7/6/2023, noted that the site access road had E and S issues that needed to be addressed. The E and S BMP's had not been maintained and surface water runoff was not being properly conveyed away from the site. This resulted in multiple areas of standing/ponded water. Inspection #3591431, conducted on 7/26/2023, noted that the operator had dug in turnouts to drain the specific areas of standing/ponded water and placed stone/gravel to stabilize these locations. These actions were minimal and areas that are not stabilized remained. The operator has placed more gravel on the access road in an attempt to stabilize, but has not re-installed the E and S BMP's along the access road and surface water runoff is still not being conveyed away from the access road. The operator's failure to re-install the E and S BMP's in order to prevent erosion and maintain stabilization on the access road has resulted in violation being cited. Violations of 25 PA Code 78.53, 25 PA Code 102.4(b)(1), 25 PA Code 102.11(a)(1), and 25 PA Code 102.22(a) are being cited for this inspection.

The gas bubbling is not visible due to the water level being below the top of the 11 ¿ ¾¿ by 16¿ casing annulus at the time of the inspection. After reviewing ECHELONs evaluations and interpretations, and PGE 37-063-31807 1025 well completion report. Several coal seams and a couple freshwater aquafers were encountered before the casing seat of the surface string. There are freshwater aquafers noted on the well completion report at 83¿ and 130¿ and coal at 27¿ 83¿ 127¿ 152¿ 155¿ and 338¿. The depth of 11-3/4¿ casing is at 568.6¿, a couple hundred feet below the deepest coal. The report identifies the gas source behind the surface casing and a potential to comingle with the identified water aquifers. The Department is denying PGE any request to vent the gas from the 11-3/4¿ x 16¿ annulus as a permeant repair solution. As per 78.86 PGE is required to submit a plan to remediate the issue and has failed to do so. Also, within 30 days of receiving the inspection report, the Department is requesting any Logs or previous predrill data associated with the well.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On November 29, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at the Beech Resources ISA Well Pad. At the time of inspection, Beech Resources was in stimulation operations of the recently drilled wells. An area of elevated soil conductivity was observed off the west end of the well pad in an area that was recently backfilled due to a developed erosion channel. The DEP screened the surrounding area and found the area of elevated conductivity to be approximately 180 ft. x 30 ft. This area encompasses the top of the well pad slope down past the compost filter socks in place and about 20 ft. past the compost filter sock. Soil conductivity in the area of impact ranged from 1,500 uS/cm to over range reading of the soil conductivity meter. The upper limit of the soil conductivity meter is 4,000 uS/cm. Soil sample 0651-141 was collected from the area of impact. During the inspection, Don Stevenson with Beech Resources arrived onsite. DEP showed Mr. Stevenson where the area of elevated conductivity was found off the west end of the pad slope. While DEP was still onsite, Mr. Stevenson called to have an excavator sent to the well pad. Mr. Stevenson said Penn E and R was also called to schedule a time to delineate the spill. Due to the unknown volume of the spill, Beech Resources plans to clean up the area under the Act 2 remediation requirments. During the inspection, another area was observed off the southwest corner of the well pad where an erosion channel had formed at the top of the well pad slope and continued down past the compost filter sock off the permitted limit of disturbance. This area was also shown to Mr. Stevenson and he said that Beech Resources will dress up compost filter socks and backfill the channel that has formed.Much of the site has become vegetated. Temporary E and S controls are still in place and are in good condition except for the previously mentioned areas.The area of elevated levels of conductivity outside of containment off the well pad edge is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b). Additional violations could be assessed pending results from the soil sample collected. An erosion channel has formed at the top of the well pad slope and continues off the permitted limit of disturbance conveying sediment off the permitted site is an additional violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b) and Chapter 102.11(a)1.

Comments: On June 24, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad.All areas that had been excavated off of the well pad due to the spill have been back filled and regraded. These areas have not been reseeded or temporarily stabilized. The DEP recommends temporarily stabilizing the recently rebuilt infiltration berms and pad slope, if reseeding the area is not planned in the future to prevent accelerated erosion of the area. The DEP also recommends areas of the permitted site that have not achieved the 70% uniform, perennial vegetative covered be reseeded. Two monitoring wells were observed drilled off to the west of the pad about 50 yards. There has not been any remediation of the well pad to date.About 8 inches of water was in the southwest stormwater vault. The water was not high enough in this vault to be measured for conductivity due to not being able to reach the water levels with the field water quality meter. There was about 12 inches of water in the northwest stormwater vault and the water was not high enough in the vault to be able to screen for conductivity with the water quality meter.The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 20.5 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 20.8 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 24.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 24.2 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 99. 6 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 100.7 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 29.8 uS/cm. Seep 3 was dry and a conductivity screening could not be completed. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 108.1 uS/cm. Seep 5 was dry and a conductivity screening could not be completed. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers.Infiltration berms 4, 6, and 7 appear to be holding water and not infiltrating within 72 hours. The DEP recommend investigating into the functionality of these berms to avoid over topping or berm erosion.No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-06-02
Comments: On June 2, 2020, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection as a response to a reported production fluid spill at Beech Resources Premier Pad. DEP received a phone call from Don Stevenson with Beech Resources reporting a spill of around 400 gallons of production fluid from the GPU onsite. A dump line valve on the GPU recently failed and was replaced. Within the next couple days vegetation downslope from the GPU was noticed to be dead. How the production fluid was spilled is still being determined. At the time of the inspection, the operator was in the process of excavating the impacted soil. There are two strips of impacted soil, they are about equal in size. The impacted area is about 10 ft wide by 90 ft long. At the top of the slope, the excavator had dug up about 3 ft deep of soil. Soil conductivity in the right strip of dead vegetation ranged from 700 uS/cm to over range readings of the meter, which is 4,000 uS/cm. The impacted soil is still within the LOD so no production fluid left the permitted LOD. Beech Resources plans to follow the Act 2 remediation. The spill of production fluid outside of containment is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), §78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Outstanding violations from Inspection No. 3001824 still remain.
